subject: [PATCH v8 14/30] mm: zswap: reject high-order swap cache allocations backed by zswap

2026-10-02.patch_summary: This patch rejects high-order swap cache allocations backed by zswap when the range of swap slots is split between zswap entries and the backing device. This prevents a disk read from returning stale or zero data for every slot zswap owns. The check is done after the folio is in the swap cache, ensuring that the answer is stable. If a high-order allocation over such a range is attempted, it will be rejected with an -EBUSY error.

reviews.author: Yosry Ahmed
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested splitting the patch into three separate patches, one of which does not need to be part of the current series.

Reviewer Yosry Ahmed suggested refactoring the code into a separate patch, and specifically requested that this patch only contain the logical change related to rejecting high-order allocations if any entry is in zswap.

Reviewer suggested avoiding function name references that may become outdated, and instead listed alternative ways of 'pinning' a range; also proposed splitting the changes to mm/zswap.c into a separate patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Overall looks good, but I think it can be split into 3 patches (one of
which doesn't have to be part of this series), see below.

---

Nit: You can pull the refactoring into a separate patch (as well as
most zswap changes, see below), so that this patch only has the
logical change to bail for higher orders if any entry is in zswap.

---

I would rather avoid naming specific functions as it will go stale
quickly, and instead list the ways of "pinning" a range.

Also, generally, the changes to mm/zswap.c seem orthogonal to this
patch and can be a separate patch (which would be clearer if
__swap_cache_alloc() isn't named here).

2026-10-05.patch_summary: This patch rejects high-order swap cache allocations backed by zswap when the range of swap slots is split between zswap entries and the backing device. This prevents a disk read from returning stale or zero data for every slot owned by zswap. The check is performed after the folio is in the swap cache, ensuring that the answer is stable. If a high-order allocation over such a range is attempted, an error is returned. The patch also exports the zswap_is_present() function for use by PMD-order swap-in users.
